[i]This is a review of only the main campaign on Normal difficulty because I did not enjoy the game enough to attempt to play other modes or replay the campaign on harder difficulties.[/I]

[i]Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine[/i] is a good game that occasionally pales on its own premise, especially for most of its final third.

This is basically a horde shooter with occasional melee, and it's at its most fun when the protagonist, [I]Titus[/I], is given powerful guns, melee weapons, or a flying jetpack and mowing down hordes of [I]Orcs[/I] and [I]Soldiers of Chaos[/I].

There's a fairly well-conceived tactical element to the chaos: managing ammo, grenades, super meter, health, enemy prioritization, and positional awareness are key to survival.

As fun as it can be at its best, the game has a number of issues:
[olist]
[*] You cannot hold all weapons at all times, and the game has a habit of forcing you to alternate through weapons mainly because you ran out of ammo. Issue is: there's no way for you to know if the weapon you're picking up is a good fit for the fights ahead, so you may occasionally end up in situations where your loadout is categorically ill-suited.
[*] The previous issue is compounded by the introduction of the most powerful melee weapon: the [I]Thunder Hammer[/I], which happens to disable 2 out of 4 ranged weapon slots, where the most powerful guns/rifles typically live. I assume to balance difficulty, the game makes it impossible to simultaneously use the most powerful melee and ranged weapons, which severely limits the fun.
[*] For the first 3 quarters of the final third of the game, ammo sporadically gets scarce, and the game places [I]Titus[/I] in closed arenas with covers and enemies on high, often unreachable, platforms and introduces flying enemies. I assume this is done to introduce gameplay variety. What it unfortunately also does is eliminate melee as a viable offensive option and force the player to approach these segments as if the game is a tactical shooter, which can get tedious quickly.
[*] The game's idea of boss fights is painfully lackluster. Throughout the campaign, there are basically 2 bosses who reappear to either taunt or beat [I]Titus[/I] in cutscenes and disappear with a promise of a boss fight to come. [i]Titus[/i] is thrown into a dark, fairly tight arena with 1 boss and his hordes, and the other boss fight is a trivial quick time sequence.
[/olist]
[i]Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine[/I] has really high highs as a horde shooter; however, at times, it feels almost as if the game was developed by 2 separate teams with diametrically opposing ideas. There's probably more to optimize and mine out of the mechanics and campaign if you're a horde shooter fanatic, but the flaws outweigh the fun if you're not committed enough to the genre.
A good legacy game. First played it as a kid back around 2016. Never got to complete it. Now I have.

The story is amazing, the gameplay is fun and the music is great.

The side stories told by the servo skulls add much to the hopeless atmosphere of 40k that is often missing while playing as a space marine, really do recommend looking for them.

The only big downside of this game is seen IF you've played Space Marine 2 first, as the sound design there is much better, making you seem quite light and your weapons weak in this one.

PEAK.
